attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. The tweets he quotes (LeCun, Chapman) are not part of the claim.

semantics.note: Reading 'prevaricates. A lot.' as 'frequently produces false or fabricated content' matches the context about confabulated math and science. The statement is unhedged, so it is a plain observation.

contract.note: Marcus gives no measure. The plain reading (a recurring, substantial problem at launch, with no deceptive intent required) is fair and ordinary. It neither asks for a majority-false rate nor counts a single error as enough.

evidence.note: Firsthand prompts and outputs dated Nov 15, 2022. Ordinary questions about the gravitational constant and Venus transits got many fabricated facts: wrong biographies, false mission history, gibberish transit dates. Errors recur across several ordinary prompts.
The developers report low absolute TruthfulQA accuracy. That is a benchmark result, not a fabrication rate in demo outputs, and the testing dates are unspecified.
The paper abstract reports benchmark successes. These show the model was not uniformly wrong, but they do not show that fabrication was rare in generated responses.
NASA confirms the 2012 Venus transit, which shows that Galactica's '1882 last transit' output was false. This is background fact-checking, not an observation of Galactica.

reviews.rationale: Launch-day records (e1) show repeated, substantive fabrications across several ordinary scientific prompts, not one isolated failure, which meets the support condition under a fair plain reading. The benchmark successes (e3) do not show fabrication was rare. Prevalence across representative use is not established, but the claim does not require it.
